significance: The first frozen prediction in this programme to pass as written. Twelve preceded it and all twelve failed.

setting.baseline: select -- per-step attribution at full depth, which solves the task, so the comparison is matched-accuracy

N1_accuracy_matched.required: within 0.02 of select on the mean

N2_optimal_allocation.required: mean steps within 0.5 of empirical E[distance]
N2_optimal_allocation.measured: 6.14 steps against E[d] 6.14, agreeing to two decimals

N3_small_batch_win.measured: 2.78x, mean over 25 independent examples (select 1504.3 us, arrival 541.9 us)

N4_the_boundary_reappears.note: This is the prediction that mattered. The ceiling was derived on the streaming family and had to appear unprompted here. It did, and the whole crossover curve came with it.

what_this_licenses: A scoped engineering claim WITH ITS CEILING: on workloads with a deep worst case and
heavy-tailed difficulty, supervised predicate halting delivers a 2.8-4.9x wall-clock inference
saving at batch 1, at matched accuracy and matched parameters, and loses that advantage
The niche is therefore single-stream, latency-sensitive, on-device inference. It is explicitly
NOT server-side batched serving, where the method is a 3% penalty.
what_this_does_not_license: Any novelty claim. Supervised early exit and per-step attribution are prior art; see the
Any claim that the SIZE of the saving is a property of the architecture. It is max_depth /
E[predicate index], a property of the workload. The architecture's contribution is attaining
that optimum reliably, which it does to two decimal places in every setting measured.
Any capability claim. QNEURO3-EXTRAP-P1 failed and adaptive halting buys no depth extrapolation.
Any general principle about where an answer must be read from. QNEURO3-TRANSFER-P1 failed.
the_mechanism_behind_the_ceiling: A batch cannot exit until its slowest member does, so batched cost scales with E[max halt over
the batch] rather than E[halt]. For P(k) proportional to 0.8^k on 1..32 the analytic curve is
E[max] = 4.97 at batch 1, 12.53 at 8, 20.96 at 64 and 29.42 at 1024, so the realisable saving
falls from 6.43x to 1.09x. This is a property of adaptive computation itself, not of this
architecture, and it applies equally to ACT, PonderNet, early-exit transformers and depth-routed
Continuous batching or sequence packing can recover part of it, but that is an inference-systems
technique rather than an architectural property, and it was not measured here.
